article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica dominant hybrid
Genetics: White Widow / Black Widow × Skunk #1
Breeder: Dutch Quality Seeds / Shantibaba
THC Content: Moderate to high
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , pinene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Skunk, sweet fruit, citrus, earth, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 40–50 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: September to early October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 450–500 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

White Shark belongs to a generation of marijuana genetics in which heavy resin production was itself a defining characteristic. Mature flowers can appear almost dusted in white as trichomes accumulate over densely packed calyxes, giving the cultivar a visual connection to the famous “White” family from which part of its ancestry comes. Beneath that frosting is a far less delicate personality: pungent Skunk, sweet fruit, earth, and sharp herbal notes combine with an effect that can begin surprisingly cheerful before settling into a substantial physical calm. It is classic Dutch cannabis rather than a modern dessert hybrid, with an emphasis on resin, durability, fast flowering, and unmistakable odor.

The White Shark name requires some historical context. The Dutch Quality Seeds release is closely connected to the genetic line originally created by breeder Shantibaba as Great White Shark and later maintained by Mr. Nice Seedbank under the Shark Shock name. Mr. Nice identifies that original family as White Widow—derived from Brazilian and South Indian genetics—crossed with Skunk #1. The breeder also documents indoor yields of 500–600 g/m², a roughly 40–50 day indoor flowering period, and September-to-early-October outdoor maturation. The Dutch Quality Seeds White Shark follows this same genetic foundation and was released as a feminized variety.
Genetics and Lineage

At the center of White Shark is the pairing of the Widow family with Skunk #1. Shantibaba’s original Great White Shark—subsequently renamed Shark Shock after the creation of Mr. Nice Seedbank—was bred from White Widow and Skunk #1. Mr. Nice still lists the family background as Brazilian sativa/South Indian genetics crossed with Skunk #1. In Mr. Nice terminology, the Widow line is now sold as Black Widow, which explains why the parentage may appear as either White Widow × Skunk #1 or Black Widow × Skunk #1 depending on the source and period being discussed.

The Widow contribution is responsible for much of the cultivar’s remarkable resin potential. White Widow became famous for flowers that could accumulate a thick layer of stalked trichomes, and that tendency survives prominently in the Shark family. Skunk #1 contributes a different set of strengths: vigorous growth, compact flowering clusters, dependable production, penetrating aroma, and a generally easier cultivation profile. Combining the two created marijuana capable of producing highly resinous flowers without demanding a complicated growing routine.

Classification is less precise than the genetics themselves. White Shark is best treated as an indica/sativa hybrid rather than assigned an arbitrary modern percentage. Its dense flower structure and increasingly physical high often resemble an indica-dominant plant, yet Brazilian and Skunk ancestry contribute noticeable cerebral activity. This mixture of traits is one reason the strain can feel balanced early in the experience before becoming considerably heavier later.
Effects and Experience

White Shark rarely feels one-dimensional. The first portion of the high can arrive with a noticeable lift in mood, easier conversation, and an almost buoyant mental quality. Ordinary sensory experiences become more interesting, food and music can seem especially appealing, and social interaction may feel less effortful. Some phenotypes produce enough cerebral stimulation to encourage creative activity, although this cannabis strain is generally less restless than a long-flowering Haze or tropical sativa.

Physical weight develops more clearly once the initial mental peak begins to stabilize. Warm relaxation may spread through the shoulders and limbs, gradually slowing the pace without necessarily producing immediate sleepiness. The progression can make the cultivar suitable for late-afternoon or evening use when the goal is to transition from activity into relaxation. With larger amounts, however, the balance can tilt decisively toward a heavy stone.

That delayed increase in body effects is worth respecting. Consumers who judge the experience only a few minutes after inhalation may take more than necessary and discover that the second half is much stronger than expected. Historical Shark Shock examples are widely described as calming, happy, and physically relaxing, while contemporary grower reports continue to note a warm body onset followed by a mellow, dreamy headspace.
Medical Benefits

White Shark’s effect profile may appeal to medical marijuana consumers looking for a combination of mood elevation and physical relaxation. Stress, temporary low mood, tension, and difficulty unwinding are among the situations in which a balanced THC-dominant hybrid may feel useful to some individuals.

The stronger body component can also make the strain attractive to consumers seeking temporary relief from everyday aches or muscular tightness. Appetite stimulation may emerge as the high progresses, particularly at larger doses. Because these responses depend heavily on the individual, the same weed that feels calming to one consumer may produce dizziness, anxiety, dry mouth, rapid thoughts, or excessive sedation in another.

Cannabinoid testing is particularly important when White Shark is being considered for medical use. There is no universal THC percentage that defines the cultivar, and flower sold under the same strain name can vary substantially according to phenotype and cultivation method. Medical decisions should therefore rely on the actual product’s laboratory analysis and qualified medical guidance rather than the name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Skunk announces itself quickly in White Shark. Mature flowers can release an unusually strong odor even before being broken apart, combining musky cannabis, damp earth, sweet fruit, and a sharp botanical edge. The Widow side adds complexity rather than simply more pungency, introducing lighter citrus, floral, and occasionally menthol-like impressions around the heavier Skunk base.

Grinding the buds tends to intensify the earthy and sour dimensions. Sweet-and-sour fruit can emerge beneath the musk, followed by herbs, pepper, and hints of fresh wood. The flavor begins smoother than the aroma might suggest, often opening with sweetness or citrus before developing a deeper earthy-Skunk finish. The original genetic line is specifically described by its breeder as exceptionally aromatic, and consumer descriptions of related Shark Shock material frequently add sweet fruit to that foundation.

No definitive terpene analysis exists for the original White Shark breeding stock. Myrcene, pinene, beta-caryophyllene, and limonene are plausible compounds in individual batches, but assigning a fixed dominant terpene to every plant would go beyond the available evidence. Growing conditions, phenotype selection, harvest maturity, and curing can all shift the final aromatic chemistry.
Growing Information

White Shark earned much of its early reputation by being straightforward to cultivate. The plant normally develops a compact, sturdy frame with strong branches capable of supporting dense, resin-heavy flowers. Internodal spacing is generally manageable indoors, and the Skunk influence encourages vigorous vegetative growth without the excessive stretch associated with many sativa varieties. Its durability makes the cultivar reasonable for newer growers while still offering enough production potential to interest experienced cultivators.

The documented indoor flowering window is unusually short at approximately 40–50 days, with expected production in the range of 500–600 grams per square meter under optimized conditions. Outdoors, mature plants have historically been listed around 450–500 grams each, with harvest occurring from September into early October in the Northern Hemisphere. Mr. Nice describes the underlying Shark genetics as extremely hardy and particularly well suited to greenhouse cultivation.

Dense flowers require attention as harvest approaches. Heavy resin production and tight calyx formation can trap moisture inside the canopy when humidity remains high, making strong airflow essential. Removing unnecessary interior growth can improve air movement while directing energy toward well-lit flowering sites. Sea of Green cultivation suits the plant’s fast finish, while topping and low-stress training work well when growers prefer fewer plants with broader canopies.

Nutrition generally does not need to be pushed aggressively. Healthy plants can support substantial flower weight when provided with consistent light, adequate root space, and balanced fertility. Outdoors, its relatively early finish gives White Shark an advantage in temperate climates because flowers can mature before prolonged autumn rain becomes severe. That combination of speed, resilience, resin, and yield explains why the original Shark line developed such a strong reputation among growers.
FAQ
What are the genetics of White Shark?

The Dutch Quality Seeds White Shark is based on the original Great White Shark/Shark Shock genetic family created by Shantibaba. The core cross is White Widow, now represented as Black Widow in the Mr. Nice catalog, crossed with Skunk #1.
Is White Shark the same as Great White Shark?

The names are closely connected but should not always be treated as interchangeable across every breeder. Shantibaba originally introduced Great White Shark and later maintained the genetics at Mr. Nice Seedbank as Shark Shock. Dutch Quality Seeds subsequently offered White Shark as a feminized version tied to that same genetic family.
Is White Shark indica or sativa?

White Shark is an indica/sativa hybrid. Its compact growth, dense flowers, and strong body relaxation frequently give it an indica-like character, while the Widow and Skunk heritage contributes a noticeable cerebral and uplifting component.
What does White Shark weed taste like?

The strain combines strong Skunk and earthy flavors with sweet fruit, citrus, herbs, spice, and occasional menthol-like freshness. Its aroma can be extremely pungent, so odor control is important during indoor cultivation.
How long does White Shark take to flower?

The documented indoor flowering period is approximately 40–50 days. Outdoor plants in the Northern Hemisphere typically finish during September or early October, making it relatively quick compared with many hybrid cannabis strains .
Final Thoughts on White Shark

White Shark comes from a period when breeders measured success through far more than cannabinoid percentages. A cultivar needed to grow reliably, finish on schedule, produce substantial flower, carry a memorable aroma, and deliver an experience strong enough to earn repeat attention. The combination of Widow resin production and Skunk #1 vigor accomplished precisely that, producing compact marijuana flowers that can become so heavily covered in trichomes that the White Shark name seems entirely appropriate.

Its enduring appeal lies in that old-school balance. The aroma moves between pungent Skunk, earth, sweet fruit, and fresh herbal notes; the high travels from upbeat mental effects into a warmer physical stone; and the plant itself can deliver substantial yields after a surprisingly short flowering cycle. Although names such as White Shark, Great White Shark, and Shark Shock have become tangled over decades of cannabis breeding, their shared history leads back to Shantibaba’s influential Widow × Skunk work. For growers and consumers interested in classic Dutch genetics, White Shark remains a useful example of why that combination became so widely respected.
